sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Out-of-Gauge (OOG) Heavy Industrial Project Cargo Logistics

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Napoleonic tradition); unitary national jurisdiction without sub-state commercial legislation
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Belgo-Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU) bilateral investment treaty programme (approximately 90 BITs)
Luxembourg-Germany DTAA and bilateral investment protection arrangements
Luxembourg-United States income tax treaty (1996, as amended by 2004 and 2009 protocols)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Loi modifiée du 12 novembre 2004 relative à la lutte contre le blanchiment et contre le financement du terrorisme (AML/CFT law, as amended by the Law of 25 March 2020 transposing Directive (EU) 2015/849 and (EU) 2018/843); Loi du 13 janvier 2019 établissant le registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (UBO Register law), as amended by Loi du 24 mars 2023 following CJEU judgments C-37/20 and C-601/20; Règlement grand-ducal du 27 mai 2019 relatif au registre des bénéficiaires effectifs; Article 710-1 et seq. of the Loi du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales (SARL); Law of 19 December 2002 on the commerce and companies register (RCS/LBR).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Statuts) of the SARL executed as notarial deed
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg civil-law notary (Chambre des Notaires du Grand-Duché de Luxembourg)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarial authentic act (no apostille needed for domestic effect); registration with RCS/LBR

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing of each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry of the shareholder's country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (1961 Hague Convention for contracting states) OR consular legalization by the Luxembourg diplomatic or consular post for non-convention states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney (procuration) authorizing signature of the incorporation deed
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate shareholder (board resolution) or individual principal
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, plus sworn translation into French or German if the document is issued in a non-Luxembourg language

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO Declaration and ownership-chain organizational chart (Déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Signature before the notary or sworn declaration; electronically filed with the RBE within one month of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank attestation of blocked funds (attestation de blocage de fonds) covering at least 25% pay-up of the EUR 12,400 minimum subscribed capital
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg credit institution holding the blocked account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank certification; no apostille required; valid until the RCS filing and release instruction at incorporation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory integrated screening: (1) identification and verification of all shareholders, directors, managers and beneficial owners to the 25% threshold; (2) PEP classification and enhanced due diligence under Article 3(7) and Article 8 of the AML/CFT Law of 12 November 2004; (3) automated checks against the EU consolidated financial sanctions list (Council Regulation (EU) No 833/2014 and asset-freeze measures), UN Security Council consolidated list, OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists (USD clearing capacity), and Luxembourg FIU (Cellule de Renseignement Financier) restrictive measures; (4) adverse-media and sanctions screening of counterparties of the parent group for the project cargo supply chain; (5) verification of the source of funds for the paid-up capital with documentary evidence (bank statements, audited financial statements); (6) retention of all KYC/AML records for a minimum of five years after termination of the business relationship; the notary and the bank apply face-to-face or video-identification rules under the CSSF's ABBL-CSSF guidance; no waiver of CDD because the ISIC 5229 business is classified Low Risk Standard.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS); portal www.lbr.lu; electronic incorporation via MyGuichet/eluxtrust with the interlocking notarial filing
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name may be expressed in any European Union official language, but must be written in Latin characters and must be distinguishable from all names already registered in the RCS. The name must necessarily be followed by the suffix 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' or the abbreviation 'S.à r.l.' / 'SARL'. French is the controlling language of the statuts; if the name uses a non-understandable language, a French or German translation of the name and statuts must be supplied to the RCS and the notary. Names that are identical or confusingly similar to a prior registered trade name are refused; purely descriptive logistics terms such as 'Cargo', 'Heavy Haul' and 'Project Logistics' are admissible when combined with a unique distinctive element.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: State/public-authority terms: Etat, National, Municipal, Commune, Grand-Duché (reserved for public bodies and requiring ministerial authorization)
Banking tokens: Banque, Caisse d'épargne (reserved for licensed credit institutions under CSSF supervision)
Insurance tokens: Assurance, Réassurance (reserved for licensed undertakings)
Fund/management tokens: OPCVM, SICAV, FCP, Fonds d'investissement, Gestion de fortune, Fiduciaire (require CSSF approval)
Stock-exchange token: Bourse (reserved for licensed exchange operators)
Regulated professions: Audit, Commissaire (admission with Institut des Réviseurs d'Entreprises required)
EU-institution tokens: Européen, Union européenne (misleading implication of official EU character)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Luxembourg law does not provide a pre-emptive statutory name reservation; the notary verifies the chosen name at RCS/LBR on the day of signature and the name is secured by filing the incorporation dossier. No extension mechanism exists; re-filing of the same or a similar name is possible at any time. Upon rejection for identity or confusing similarity, the notary amends the draft statuts by adding a distinguishing element (e.g., geographic or project descriptor), and the instrument is re-submitted to the RCS. The applicant may alternatively lodge an administrative appeal with the Minister of Justice within three months under the Law of 19 December 2002 on commercial registers, and a judicial annulment action before the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg (commercial chamber) within the same period. Amended re-filings are exempt from additional registration tax if made within 30 days.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Partially permissible. The SARL must have a registered office (siège social) in the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg (Article 710-1 of the Law of 10 August 1915). Domiciliation through an approved domiciliation agent is lawful under the Law of 31 May 1999, as amended. However, the Luxembourg tax administration and the AEDT require genuine economic substance for a logistics project-cargo operator: local premises, staff, management and decision-making. A purely virtual office without operational presence may be accepted at registration but will be challengeable in VAT, customs and corporate income tax audits.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 15-20% aggregate probability within the first three fiscal years. The RCS/LBR does not conduct physical inspections; unannounced controls are not routine for a low-risk logistics SARL. The Luxembourg customs administration (Administration des douanes et accises) may perform site inspections for heavy-haul project cargo movements, and the income tax authority may conduct substance reviews; such visits are usually intelligence-driven and focused on VAT/transfer-pricing substance rather than random inspection of registered offices.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Minimum paid-in capital contribution (25% of EUR 12,400 subscribed minimum capital; refundable company asset, not a fee)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg credit institution (blocked account in the name of the SARL in formation)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Article 710-1 et seq. of the Law of 10 August 1915; statutory 25% pay-up requirement, verified by attestation de blocage de fonds

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial fees for incorporation deed, name-clearance verification and RCS formalities
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg civil-law notary (tariff of the Chambre des Notaires)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff schedule; prevailing market benchmark for a standard SARL incorporation with registered capital at legal minimum

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS/LBR registration filing and RESA official gazette publication
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), RCS de Luxembourg
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: LBR fee schedule; EUR 19 electronic filing fee plus RESA (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations) publication costs

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Amended Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Title IV governing Sociétés à Responsabilité Limitée (Articles 100 et seq.); Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 23 June 1983 on special and exceptional transports for the underlying heavy-haul activity.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), Ministry of Justice.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Authentic notarial deed of incorporation (acte de constitution) together with the articles of association (statuts), filed electronically through the LBR eJustice portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Since the 2016 Luxembourg company-law reform, the SARL has no statutory minimum share capital; however, the articles must fix a stated capital with a nominal par value per share, and the full subscribed capital must be paid up and deposited into a blocked bank account ('attestation de blocage') with a Luxembourg credit institution before the notarial deed is executed. The blocked funds may not be released until the RCS registration certificate is issued. No state escrow account is imposed by law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST RESOLUTIONS OF LU SARL (Société à Responsabilité Limitée). 1. CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION: The shareholders confirm subscription to the entire issued share capital of EUR 12,000, represented by shares of EUR 100 each, and instruct the Manager to deposit the full amount on the Company's blocked account with a Luxembourg credit institution. 2. REGISTERED OFFICE: The registered office is fixed at 1, Rue Gabriel Lippmann, L-5365 Munsbach, Grand Duchy of Luxembourg. 3. MANAGEMENT: Mr./Ms. [name] is appointed sole Manager (Gérant) with sole signature, the Company being validly bound by the Manager's signature alone. 4. ADMINISTRATION: The Manager is authorized to file the deed with the RCS, publish the notice in the RESA, and effect all VAT, social security and administrative registrations. Resolved unanimously by the shareholders.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Incorporation Name Clearance and Drafting of the Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RCS name databank; Luxembourg notary (drafting)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Search the RCS/LBR registers to confirm the corporate name is available and not confusingly similar to existing registrations; instruct the notary to prepare the statuts covering name, registered office, corporate object limited to ISIC 5229 project-cargo logistics, share capital, and the gérant's powers; collect signed mandates from shareholders and UBO declarations.
required_dossiers: Copy of passports or national IDs of all shareholders and UBOs
Recent proof of address (utility or bank statement)
Name-availability excerpt from the RCS/LBR
Draft articles of association prepared by the notary
Signed notary mandate and UBO declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for similarity, select the next ranked alternative name, adjust the draft statuts, and re-run the name check; no notarial deed has yet been executed, so no formal setback occurs.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of the Blocked Capital Account and Deposit of Share Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution (bank) acting under CSSF AML/CFT rules
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a 'société en formation' account in the proposed corporate name, deposit the subscribed share capital, and instruct the bank to issue a blocking certificate ('attestation de blocage') stating the amount, currency, and holder; the certificate is to be remitted to the notary for the incorporation deed.
required_dossiers: Bank account opening forms and KYC questionnaire
Valid passport of shareholders and of the intended gérant
Draft articles of association
Business plan for OOG heavy-haul logistics
Evidence of source of funds and UBO status (AML)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank contests the beneficial ownership or source of funds, provide supplementary explanations and account statements; if the file is still declined, open the account with another Luxembourg bank and restart the blocking certificate procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Notarial Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Public Notary (notaire) in the jurisdiction of Luxembourg City
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the shareholders before the notary (or through valid proxies) to execute the 'acte de constitution'; the notary verifies the share subscription, capital deposit certificate, legal basis, and the manager's acceptance of office; the authentic deed is then remitted to the RCS by the notary via the eJustice portal.
required_dossiers: Final statuts approved by the shareholders
Bank capital blocking certificate
Identity documents of shareholders and the gérant
Written acceptance of office signed by the gérant
Lease or domiciliation agreement for the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any irregularity appears, the notary executes a rectification addendum before filing; any defect in the signatures is cured by a supplemental authentic act, and the corrected deed is submitted to the RCS.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS Registration and Legal Publication in the RESA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) – Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), electronic filing window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarial deed, the registration form (fiche de renseignements), and the gérant disclosures through the eJustice/LBR portal; pay the registration and publication fees; the RCS verifies compliance and assigns the RCS number; the incorporation notice is published in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA).
required_dossiers: Authentic PDF of the notarial deed
Completed RCS registration sheet
Identity and specimen signature of the gérant
Proof of payment of state fees
Power of attorney if lodged by counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS returns observations, the counsel resubmits corrected documents within the set deadline; if no response is given within 15 working days, a new application is filed with an explanatory letter, and the registration date adjusts to the second filing date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, Social Security, and Administrative Post-Registration Formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AED); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS); commune of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company for VAT with the AED via form 10 and request a Luxembourg VAT number; enrol the company as employer with the CCSS; confirm the office premises for municipal occupational/fire-safety compliance. For heavy-haul operations, each exceptional convoy separately applies for the route permit with the Roads Administration; no standing statutory license is attached to the logistics corporate vehicle.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract (extract 2)
Articles of association and incorporation deed
Lease contract or annual domiciliation renewal
Bank statement of the corporate account
Projected turnover and hiring summary for the CCSS and AED files
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AED challenges the VAT date, file the identification complement and adjust the effective VAT registration date; if late CCSS registration is noted, the employer submits regularization declarations and no sanctions are applied if no salaries were yet paid.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Administration des routes (Roads Administration) of the Ministry of Mobility and Public Works, exceptional transport permitting unit; CGDIS and Labour and Mines Inspectorate (ITM) for physical and occupational safety clearances.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No permanent industrial operating licence applies to non-regulated project-cargo logistics; the company secures per-movement 'Autorisation de transport exceptionnel' (exceptional transport authorization) under the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 23 June 1983 for OOG/heavy-haul convoys.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from mandatory EIA for pure logistics/service activities; an environmental permit under the 'commodo-incommodo' regime (Law of 21 March 2012) is required only if the undertaking operates a classified storage yard, depot, or maintenance installation exceeding the applicable thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process emissions for office-based freight logistics; for any yard or workshop, compliance is required with municipal wastewater discharge standards (no industrial pollutant without pre-treatment), EU Stage IV/V emission standards for non-road mobile machinery, particle-filter requirements for heavy equipment, and waste handling through a licensed waste collector with waste tracking forms.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety clearance by the communal authority with CGDIS certifying building evacuation, fire alarms, and extinguishers; structural stability certificate of any leased warehouse or yard; occupational health and safety inspection by the ITM (Inspection du travail et des mines) covering internal regulations, first-aid equipment, safe load-handling procedures, and the annual risk assessment under Article L.312-1 of the Luxembourg Labour Code.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and registration; Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for corporate income tax; Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) for business registration; unified e-portal: MyGuichet.lu (guichet.lu).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A newly incorporated SARL is registered by the notary with the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), obtaining the national matricule / business number, which serves as the base TIN for all tax filings. The SARL must then file VAT registration form 645 with the AEDT (via MyGuichet.lu) to obtain the Luxembourg VAT identification number (format 'LU' + 8 digits). Non-resident foreign entities without a Luxembourg establishment performing taxable supplies in Luxembourg must register directly with the AEDT and, if established outside the EU, appoint an approved Luxembourg tax representative. The SOPARFI holding regime is confirmed through the company's constitutional object and compliance statement, not a separate registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not operate a check-the-box classification. Available elections: (i) VAT grouping (assujetti unique) election under Art. 60 of the VAT Law for 95%-controlled integrated entities; (ii) fiscal integration (tax unity) election for a 95%-owned Luxembourg subsidiary consolidation for corporate income tax; (iii) participation-exemption application for qualifying 10% holdings (or EUR 1.2M acquisition cost); and (iv) ATAD anti-hybrid election/notification for hybrid mismatch arrangements. No pass-through or transparent status is available for SARL.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (TVA - Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Non-resident suppliers: EUR 0 / no threshold - registration is mandatory for any taxable B2B or B2C supply or distance sale into Luxembourg; resident small enterprises: EUR 35,000 annual turnover franchise exemption (optional and never available to non-established foreign entities under Art. 55bis VAT Law).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, mandatory digital stamping, or continuous transaction control regime is currently enforced in Luxembourg. E-invoicing follows EU VAT Directive rules: both paper and structured electronic invoicing (EDI, XML, PDF) are accepted; VAT returns and recapitulative statements (ESL) must be filed electronically via the AEDT MyGuichet.lu eFiling portal with mandatory monthly/quarterly periodicity depending on annual turnover; Intrastat reporting applies above EU turnover thresholds. Luxembourg is preparing a future mandatory structured e-invoicing framework, but no operative API clearance gateway exists as of the current effective tax period.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rated export of goods under Art. 44(I)(1)(a) VAT Law where goods are dispatched or transported outside the European Union by the supplier or a third party acting on the supplier's behalf within 90 days of supply. Directly related international logistics services (OOG heavy-haul project cargo transport, loading, securing, handling, and freight forwarding) linked to the physical export movement also qualify for 0% VAT, provided the supplier holds documentary evidence of the transport to a third-country destination. Exports through an approved customs warehouse (regime 51/53), followed by external transit (T1), are eligible where the customs export declaration is lodged with Luxembourg Customs and the exit is confirmed.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD / EX form) accepted by Luxembourg Customs, with MRN of export
Bill of Lading (seaway/ocean) or CMR waybill confirming physical exit from EU customs territory to third country
Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT MT103 evidencing receipt of export proceeds
Commercial invoice, contract of carriage, and proof of insurance for OOG heavy-haul cargo
Cargo securing and stowage survey reports supporting the transport service nature
VAT recapitulative statement and export journal evidencing zero-rated supply
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg AEDT and Customs may reassess zero-rated exports where the supplier fails to obtain proof of exit within the statutory 3-month period, restoring standard 16% VAT plus late-payment interest at 0.8% per month (9.6% per annum) from the due date. Fraudulent or knowingly incorrect zero-rating claims constitute tax evasion under Art. 199 of the General Tax Law (Abgabenordnung), exposing directors to fines of up to five times the evaded VAT and imprisonment terms of 8 days to 6 months; clawback assessments may be raised for 5 years (10 years in cases of evasion), with denial of deduction for related input VAT and publication of the corrective assessment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), acting within the Eurosystem and under the monetary competence of the European Central Bank (ECB); banking supervision and AML/CFT enforcement for credit institutions and electronic money institutions are exercised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg applies the euro as legal tender; exchange controls are fully abolished under EU Treaty provisions on free movement of capital. Both current-account and capital-account transactions are freely convertible, including profit repatriation, dividend distributions, loan repayments, and capital redemptions. No general license is required for FX conversion or cross-border transfers. De minimis balance-of-payments statistical reporting may apply, and payments to sanctioned or high-risk jurisdictions are constrained by EU sanctions and AML/CFT surveillance, but no convertibility or remittance restrictions apply to lawful commercial transactions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg does not impose any mandatory export proceeds repatriation, surrender, or conversion obligation. Exporters are free to invoice and receive payments in any currency, hold foreign-currency accounts, and convert or maintain balances without statutory timelines or mandatory conversion ratios. The only obligations are accounting, tax documentation, and compliance with EU sanctions and AML/CFT rules.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État, Luxembourg (BCEE / Spuerkeess)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium for ancillary settlement, low-value sourcing, and expense flows; Low for primary receivables and high-value project cargo disbursements. Legal constraints: an EEA-licensed electronic money institution (EMI) may provide services in Luxembourg on a cross-border services passport or through a CSSF-authorised branch; non-EEA offshore EMIs without a passport cannot lawfully undertake payment services for Luxembourg entities without CSSF authorisation. Additional constraints include client-fund safeguarding, no credit-taking, and elevated AML/KYC expectations. For heavy-haul project logistics, an EMI is acceptable only as an auxiliary rail, never as the sole clearing channel.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg's CSSF AML/CFT framework permits remote client onboarding using qualified electronic identification and video-verification procedures under an appropriate risk-based approach. In practice, most incumbent banks require an in-person interview at their premises or before a Luxembourg notary for at least one natural-person authorised signatory and usually the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO); remote opening is possible for low-risk entities and selected digital banks, but a hybrid process is standard for a SARL with cross-border project-cargo exposure and inbound capital injections: remote AML pre-screening plus physical face-to-face interview with the managing director and UBO at account opening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Holding-company structure with non-resident UBOs and multi-layer ownership
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized and apostilled certificate of incorporation; certificate of good standing; up-to-date shareholders' register and UBO declaration filed with the Luxembourg trade and companies register (RCSL); full corporate tree with jurisdictional rationale; board resolution appointing authorised signatories; professional reference from a regulated EU financial institution; audited financial statements or opening balance sheet.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value cross-border project cargo payments to third parties in geographies with perceived sanctions exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed project logistics, construction, or sales contracts naming the beneficiaries; commercial invoices and bills of lading / CMR waybills; shipping and customs documentation; supplier due-diligence file including licenses, ownership, and sanctions screening; evidence that no sanctioned person has a beneficial interest; narrative justification for each wire underlying the genuine trade.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual payment frequency or large milestone wires inconsistent with working capital
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Project timeline and milestone schedule; cash-flow forecast; agreed commercial milestone triggers; client invoice register; prior bank statements; management accounts; written explanation of payment velocity acceptable to the bank's transaction-monitoring unit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Politically exposed person (PEP) or family member of PEP as shareholder or director
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PEP and fraud self-declaration; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds reports prepared by a licensed auditor or attorney; documented legitimate business background; notarized identification and proof of address; board and UBO approvals; independent compliance review by external counsel.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant SWIFT MT103 or MT202 transfers to the Luxembourg SARL's IBAN (LU plus check digits plus domestic bank code plus account number), with exact remittance information including the corporate name and purpose code. Use EU balance-of-payments purpose categories such as 'Capital Injection (INVP)', 'Direct Investment (DI)', or, if structured as shareholder debt, 'Shareholder Loan (INTR)'. Verification should include executed shareholders' meeting minutes approving the capital increase or loan agreement, notarised subscription certificates, RCSL filing evidence, updated share register, and the contributor's full KYC pack. For third-country transfers exceeding EUR 10,000, the bank may require economic-substance evidence or a declaration under Luxembourg administrative practice. Funds routed through crypto intermediaries or clearance houses will be rejected.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For euro-denominated payments within SEPA, use SEPA Credit Transfer with the beneficiary's EUR IBAN; for non-euro or outside-EEA settlements, use SWIFT MT103 (customer transfer) with detailed transaction narrative and purpose codes tied to trade settlement. For capital-intensive equipment purchases, the primary clearing rail is an irrevocable, confirmed documentary credit (UCP 600) opened through a Luxembourg clearing bank, with documents routed through the freight forwarder. Supplier payments may also be executed via MT202 or nostro account transfers. All outbound disbursements must be grounded in underlying contracts to satisfy bank transaction-monitoring and EU sanctions screening.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX spot contracts (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/CHF and other major convertibles)
Outright currency forwards with physical settlement, tenors up to 24 months
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on non-convertible or restricted currencies for hedging project-cargo receivables
Cross-currency swaps (fixed-floating and floating-floating, EUR vs USD or other major pairs) for multi-year asset exposure
Plain-vanilla FX options (call/put) and zero-cost collar structures, subject to ISDA 2002 and appropriate OTC derivative eligibility
Currency swaps under CSA/ISDA, including cross-currency interest rate swaps, when justified by long-term project financing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting (AGM) approving financial statements and discharging the manager (gérant)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders; minutes kept in the corporate Minute Book at the registered office (no filing to a public authority)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the close of the financial year; for a calendar-year SARL, by 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Manager liability and court-compelled AGM upon shareholder petition; persistent failure to approve accounts blocks the RCS filing and may trigger strike-off proceedings before the Luxembourg District Court

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts (balance sheet, profit and loss account, notes, directors' report) filed with the Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), via the eCDF electronic filing platform
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within seven months of the financial year-end and no later than one month after AGM approval; for a calendar-year SARL, by 31 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines of EUR 500 to EUR 25,000 per officer for non-compliance with the Companies Law; publication of a default notice in the RCS; administrative strike-off and judicial dissolution initiated by the Public Prosecutor after continued default

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax (CIT) and municipal business tax (MBT) return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 December of the year following the tax year for electronic filing (standard for calendar-year companies); paper filing due by 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest of 0.6% per month on the unpaid amount; late-filing surcharge of 10% of the assessed tax; forced assessment with a 10% penalty uplift; habitual failures attract director liability and fraud procedures

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed together with the CIT/MBT return by 31 December of the following year; minimum lump-sum NWT of EUR 1,500 applies where the balance-sheet total exceeds EUR 350,000
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest at 0.6% per month; late-filing surcharge of up to 10% of assessed tax; forced assessment with a 10% uplift; failure to file may block issuance of the RCS certificate of good standing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial ownership (UBO) data in the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE), e-UBO platform
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation synchronised with the annual accounts deposit by 31 July; any change in beneficial ownership must be declared within one month of the event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines of EUR 125 to EUR 1,250 per day of continued non-compliance; criminal penalties (fine and/or imprisonment) for wilfully false declarations; suspension of dividend distributions in certain enforcement cases

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A SARL must appoint an independent statutory auditor (réviseur d'entreprises agréé) where it exceeds two of three criteria on the balance-sheet date: (i) balance-sheet total over EUR 4.4 million, (ii) net turnover over EUR 8.8 million, (iii) average of 50 employees during the financial year; the exemption is lost only after the thresholds are breached for two consecutive years.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Law of 19 December 2002 on the RCS and annual accounts, in line with the 4th EU Accounting Directive); IFRS permitted only for consolidated accounts and is optional for individual SARL accounts unless the SARL is listed or group requirements intervene

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each SARL must maintain accurate UBO profiles in the RBE; the annual confirmation is filed electronically via e-UBO together with the annual accounts and must reflect any shareholding transfer occurring during the year; UBO identification applies at the 25% plus one share direct or indirect ownership threshold; access to the RBE is restricted to competent authorities and obliged entities performing AML due diligence.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: EUR 800 to EUR 3,000 per annum for domiciliation agent services (registered office, corporate mailbox, regulatory correspondence handling)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: EUR 4,000 to EUR 15,000 per annum for an independent audit where thresholds apply; no audit fee incurred if the SARL benefits from the small-company exemption

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (Luxembourg corporate income tax 17.00% plus 7.00% unemployment fund surcharge on the CIT base plus 6.75% municipal business tax on taxable income, aggregate ordinary rate for Luxembourg City; rates vary slightly by commune)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory participation exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains on qualifying shareholdings (95% exemption, effectively 0.00% on exempt income after a 0.05% non-deductible expense allocation); 80% flat-rate notional interest deduction (NID) available on qualifying new equity; investment tax credit (8.00% of qualifying investment up to EUR 150,000, 1.50% above); IP box regime (80% exemption on qualifying IP income, effective rate 5.16% under the modified nexus approach); territorial branch exemption for qualifying foreign permanent establishments under certain conditions; group consolidation regime (intégration fiscale) allowing full offset of profits and losses among Luxembourg group members

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 470 (Corporate Income Tax Return) for standard SARL taxpayers; Form 470/RTS for entities subject to the municipal business tax (commune copy); submitted electronically via the Luxembourg direct tax e-filing portal ('eCDF' through MyGuichet.lu) or by paper filing where authorised; social security and withholding returns are separate
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Standard deadline: 31 May following the end of the tax year for taxpayers whose fiscal year coincides with the calendar year (31 December); extended automatically to 30 June; further monthly extensions available upon reasoned request (up to a maximum of 6 months, subject to a final deadline of 30 November of the following year); payments of CIT and municipal business tax are due based on quarterly provisional instalments (10 March, 10 June, 10 September, 10 December) with the final balancing payment due with the assessment notice

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Entity identification: legal form (SARL), company name, registered office address, corporate registration number (RCS), tax identification number (matricule) – preprinted by the e-filing system
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident SARL with a Luxembourg permanent establishment must indicate its foreign head-office address and obtain a Luxembourg TIN prior to filing

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax year period: start date and end date of the fiscal year (must match the articles of association unless changed by shareholder resolution)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident filer uses the Luxembourg fiscal year of the permanent establishment; where the foreign head office uses a different fiscal year, the Luxembourg PE must file based on the PE's accounting period as presented in the local books

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Basis of assessment: confirm whether the return covers a full 12-month period or a short first fiscal period
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State clearly if the PE is newly established or ceases activity mid-year; short-period returns are not prorated for tax rate purposes

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Commercial balance sheet profit/loss before tax as per Luxembourg GAAP (annual accounts)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The PE must keep and submit separate local accounts; foreign head-office accounts are not sufficient

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-back of non-deductible expenses: fines, penalties, corporate income tax itself, municipal business tax, 50% of certain entertainment expenses, excessive director fees, and payments to non-cooperative jurisdictions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All disallowed amounts incurred by the Luxembourg PE or allocated from head office must be added back; transfer pricing adjustments require simultaneous corresponding adjustments

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible items: interest subject to thin capitalisation limits, royalties, business expenses wholly and exclusively incurred for the Luxembourg business
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest on shareholder loans must satisfy the arm's length principle and the 30% EBITDA limitation; the PE may deduct only expenses attributable to the PE

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax-exempt income: participation exemption dividends and capital gains, IP box income, notional interest deduction
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders cannot apply the participation exemption to Luxembourg source dividends paid by the PE; the exemption applies only at the level of the Luxembourg corporate taxpayer

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income computation: net taxable amount after adjustments and deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Luxembourg-sourced income of the PE is taxable; foreign-sourced income is outside the PE base unless attributable under the OECD model

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits: withholding tax credits on Luxembourg source dividends/interest, foreign tax credit for taxes on foreign income included in the Luxembourg tax base
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the foreign tax credit mechanism to avoid double taxation; maximum credit equals Luxembourg CIT attributable to the same income

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Assessment of corporate income tax (17% base rate), unemployment surcharge (7% of CIT), municipal business tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Municipal business tax applies to the PE if the PE is situated in a Luxembourg commune; the surcharge and municipal tax are calculated on the same taxable base

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses available for carryforward (5 years) and loss carryback (no statutory carryback)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses of a Luxembourg PE may be carried forward only against future Luxembourg PE profits; losses of the foreign head office are not attributed to the PE

stage_6.failure_penalties: Late filing: EUR 50 to EUR 250 per month or part of a month, with a maximum of EUR 2,500, plus a 10% late payment interest charge per annum; late payment interest is computed from the first day following the statutory payment deadline; failure to file is assessed on a default assessment (imposition d'office) with a 100% to 300% penalty on the additional tax found due in case of gross negligence or intent; late provisional instalments incur interest at 0.20% per month; administrative fines up to EUR 25,000 for repeat non-compliance; criminal penalties up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment of up to 5 years for tax evasion or fraudulent filing under Luxembourg tax law.
